23 A police car travels at a velocity of 30.0 m s–1 directly towards a stationary observer. The horn of
the car emits sound of frequency 2000 Hz. The speed of sound is 340 m s–1.
What is the frequency of the sound heard by the observer?
A
1840 Hz
B
2000 Hz
C
2180 Hz
D
2190 Hz

hints: Notice the $30.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ police car is moving directly towards the stationary observer, so the observed wavelength is shortened and frequency must increase above $2000 \text{ Hz}$.
Recall the Doppler relation for a moving source and stationary observer uses the effective wavelength $(v - v_s)/f_s$ with $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Set up $f_o = v/\lambda_{obs} = f_s \times v/(v - v_s)$ with $v - v_s = 310 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and evaluate $2000 \times 340/310$.
walkthrough: Identify the data: source frequency $f_s = 2000 \text{ Hz}$, wave speed $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, source speed towards observer $v_s = 30.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, observer stationary.
State the physics: motion towards the observer crowds wavefronts together, so observed wavelength $\lambda_o = (v - v_s)/f_s$ is smaller and observed frequency $f_o = v/\lambda_o$ is larger.
Combine to the approaching-source formula: $f_o = f_s \times v/(v - v_s)$.
Substitute with units: $f_o = 2000 \text{ Hz} \times 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}/(340 - 30.0) \text{ m s}^{-1} = 2000 \times 340/310 \text{ Hz}$.
Calculate the intermediate result: $340/310 \approx 1.097$, so $f_o \approx 2000 \times 1.097 \approx 2194 \text{ Hz}$.
Round to the given options as $2190 \text{ Hz}$ and check the unit is $\text{Hz}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: This uses $v+v_s$ in the denominator and gives the lower frequency for a source moving away, not towards the observer.

B.explanation: This is the emitted $2000 \text{ Hz}$ with no Doppler shift, which ignores the $30.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ approach speed.

C.explanation: This multiplies by $(v+v_s)/v$ instead of dividing by $v-v_s$, giving about $2180 \text{ Hz}$ rather than the correct approaching-source value.

D.explanation: For approach, $f_o = f_s v/(v-v_s) = 2000 \times 340/310 \approx 2190 \text{ Hz}$, which is higher than the emitted frequency.
